Generally I'll keep my gaming head separate from my collecting head. If I found an Action 52 for really cheap I'd snag it, of course, but I can't imagine actually sitting down and playing that turd.

If the game is a cartridge game, I'll locate the ROM for it and either play it on an emulator or on the real console using an Everdrive. I consider this "borrowing a game from a friend" like we did back in the day.

I'll then evaluate on it's worth owning physically or digitally (virtual console) and make a purchasing decision, influenced by the current market pricing for the physical carts.

For example: I would very much love to snatch up a good physical cart of Mega Man 5 some day, but even when it was $65, that was too much. I settled for the ROM on my Everdrive and bought MM5 as a virtual console title on my 3DS.

Some games just aren't worth buying, so if the game sucks, or is OK enough to play once every 5 years, I'll stick with the ROM.

For example: I recently became aware of the existence of Midnight Resistance for the Genesis. Curious about it being a pseudo-Contra game that slipped under my radar back in the day, I grabbed the ROM. As it turns out, the control scheme is HORRIBLE. Even though the cart is about $20 online, it's just not worth it to me. I've kept the ROM handy for future evaluation, but bah!
